subject: Nmix.gof.test times out while testing for c-hat for pcount models

messages.author: c27b5a30c13a701e
messages.subject: Nmix.gof.test times out while testing for c-hat for pcount models
parts:
Hello all,

I have successfully calculated c-hat variance inflation factors for several of my unmarked pcount models using Nmix.gof.test in AICcmodavg. Unfortunately, for a subset of models (all of which converged when run), the Nmix.gof.test function continues to run and doesn't stop. I've tried several nsim values from n = 1000 down to nsim = 100. I've even run the gof tests with nsim = 1000 and nsim = 100 for several of the models on an HPC for a week, and they still timed out.

Here is example code:

(more complex model)

m1 <- pcount(~year + time_start + I(time_start^2) + wind ~ veg + I(veg^2) + fruit + I(fruit^2) + water + I(water^2) + drainage + I(drainage^2) + pools + I(pools^2) + dist_des + I(dist_des^2), mixture = 'NB', data = umf.stacked)

m1.gof <- Nmix.gof.test(m1, nsim = 100)

(simpler model)

m2 <- pcount(~year + dayofyear ~ neighborhood_affluence, mixture = 'NB', data = umf.stacked.2)
m2.gof <- Nmix.gof.test(m2, nsim = 100)

My question is, what is the next analytical step? Should I set a fairly arbitrary or conservative c-hat (c-hat = 1, c-hat = 4) and assess these models with a grain of salt? Or should I consider these models non-convergent and only use the set of models from which I was able to calculate c-hat?

Thanks all,

Aaron

messages.author: 4e956cc50ac3e075
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Nmix.gof.test times out while testing for c-hat for pcount models
parts:
Hi Aaron,

You don't provide much information on the size of your dataset. Do you
get sensible estimates and SE's for model m1? How long does it take to
get the solution with your original data using pcount( )? If your data
set is really large, do you have sufficient RAM? Have you tried lower
values for nsim? For example:

m1.gof <- Nmix.gof.test(m1, nsim = 5)

It might be a combination of the data set and difficulty estimating
parameters for the NB. Have you tried an alternative distribution?

Marc

messages.author: c27b5a30c13a701e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Nmix.gof.test times out while testing for c-hat for pcount models
parts:
Thank you Marc, these are all great points, and apologies for not elaborating.

Lower nsims (nsim = 5) does work for these, so it might just be moving incredibly slow (even using high performance computing with multiple cores). I think these might be overparameterized and using NB rather than P might also be an issue. The sample size is a 123 "sites" x 6 "obs" (stacked), so not large at all, the models themselves take 0 - 3 mins to run, looking now at the SEs, both models have fairly large SEs versus the estimates, and the complex model had a term that produced an NaN, which I didn't catch before.

I'm purposefully including many terms because I am model averaging, first calculating the c-hat from the overparameterized global models, and using that c-hat in the model averaging. Perhaps toning their complexity down to allow for it to work is a better idea. I'll remove terms that don't converge, and if that doesn't work I'll further simplify with P rather than NB. I'll try these iterations and see what works best.

Thanks again for your help/suggestions,

Aaron
